analysis: The code snippet calls `XMLOutputFactory.newInstance()` inside `getOrCreateOutputFactory()`. According to the provided javadoc, `newInstance()` throws `FactoryConfigurationError` if an instance of the factory cannot be loaded. In the context, before the call, the code sets the system property `javax.xml.stream.XMLOutputFactory` to `"com.ctc.wstx.stax.WstxOutputFactory"` (a Woodstox implementation). It also attempts to load a repackaged class `"ca.uhn.fhir.repackage.javax.xml.stream.XMLOutputFactory"`, but that is unrelated to the factory implementation. There is no validation or catch for `FactoryConfigurationError` around the `newInstance()` call; the method itself declares `throws FactoryConfigurationError`. The only checks in the snippet are for `ClassNotFoundException`, which is caught, but this does not prevent `FactoryConfigurationError`. Therefore, `FactoryConfigurationError` is not avoided. No other exceptions are declared in the given javadoc, so only this one is considered.
remark: The exception `FactoryConfigurationError` can be triggered if the class `com.ctc.wstx.stax.WstxOutputFactory` specified via the system property is not on the classpath or cannot be loaded. The code does not check for this condition before calling `newInstance()`, nor does it catch the error. Additionally, if the system property is not recognized or the factory class is inaccessible, a `FactoryConfigurationError` may also occur. Since there is no protective handling, the exception will propagate upward.
